title: New Neighbor
description:
Two years in the goshiwon.

A stranger washing dishes in the shared kitchen. He'd moved into room 203 that day — boxes still half-unpacked.

"Oh, hi. I just moved in today. Room 203, Park Jaewon."

26 years old. Up from Busan. First job. Same age {name} was when he first walked into this building.

{name} knows what that look means now. The one of someone who just arrived in Seoul for the first time.

choices.text: "Welcome. This room gets cold — did you bring thick blankets?" — look out for him
choices.result_text:
Jaewon smiled with relief. "Oh, really? I only packed a thin one..."

Two years ago, that was {name}'s face.

choices.text: "Take care." — short greeting, back to the room
choices.result_text:
Each went to their own room. That's how people live in goshiwons.

Still — {name} glanced back once. The kid crouched in front of his boxes.

title: Two Years Ahead
description:
Jaewon knocked on the door.

"Hey, got a minute?"

Sat and talked. ₩1.75M a month, ₩650K in rent. Didn't realize Seoul was this tight, he said. Feels like he needs to do something but doesn't know what.

"How did you start? You've been here a while, right?"

{name} thought back two years. ₩500K in the bank. ₩3B target. First year — nothing.

choices.text: "I was the same. Start by setting aside 20% of your paycheck — no exceptions." — honest advice
choices.result_text:
Jaewon wrote it down. He hadn't had anyone to tell him this.

{name} wondered what would have happened if someone had said this two years ago. But — some things you only learn by doing.

choices.text: "I still don't know much myself. Everyone's different." — keep the boundary
choices.result_text:
Jaewon looked a little deflated. {name} thought about it on the way out.

Which advice helps, which gets in the way — still not sure. So said nothing.

choices.text: Tell him everything — ₩3B, the five-year plan
choices.result_text:
Jaewon's eyes went wide. "...For real?"

Someone taking the ₩3B goal seriously. It had been a while.

title: Each to Their Own Door
description:
Boxes in the hallway.

Jaewon said he was moving to a studio apartment. Been a year. Got some breathing room and wanted more space.

"I learned a lot from you. I want to do what you're doing — you think I can?"

{name} thought back to walking this hallway for the first time two years ago. Knew nothing then.

choices.text: "You can. But — it takes longer than you think." — honest
choices.result_text:
Jaewon nodded, his expression serious.

Watched him carry the boxes down the stairs. Remembered Hyunsu leaving. The people who passed through this place — they're all gradually moving on.

Jaewon smiled and lifted his boxes. The next day, room 203's light was out.

Just {name} left.

title: Five Years Later
description:
KakaoTalk notification.

Park Jaewon. The kid from room 203.

"Hyung!! I saved ₩50M!! I kept doing what you showed me and it worked T_T"

A photo. His savings account screen. ₩52M.

{name} stared at the screen for a while. That kid who arrived crouched in front of his boxes.

choices.result_text:
"Thank you hyung!!!" Three emoji.

Leaving something behind for someone in Seoul — maybe this is what that looks like.

A neighborhood sundae gukbap place. Jaewon had changed. In a good way.

"How much are you at now, hyung?" Jaewon asked. {name} smiled. "...A little more."

Each racing toward their own number.

title: Someone Who Got There First
description:
An investment seminar. The presenter stepped up.

"Hi, I'm Lee Minseo. I started in a Gangnam jeonse apartment [rented deposit-only] at 35, and now I own the place outright. I'm 38."

[Jeonse: Korea's unique deposit-only rental system. Instead of monthly rent, you pay a large lump-sum (often ₩100M-500M+) that sits with the landlord. No monthly payments. At lease end, you get the full deposit back. It's how many Koreans 'step into' expensive areas without buying.]

Started at 35. Goal reached at 38. Three years.

{name} ran the numbers. That timeline is almost identical to his.

choices.text: Get her business card after the talk — want to ask how
choices.result_text:
Lee Minseo smiled and handed over her card.

A handshake with someone who owns a Gangnam apartment. Slightly unreal. And — she was once standing where {name} is standing.

choices.text: Just listened and left — no nerve to approach
choices.result_text:
On the way home, her words kept running through his head.

Not 'it can be done' — but 'she already did it.' That stayed longer than expected.

title: Beyond Gangnam
description:
Ran into Lee Minseo at a café near the seminar venue. Different face than on stage.

"Oh — you were at the seminar, weren't you?"

Coffee together. She said things she didn't say at the talk.

"Honestly — I got more exhausted after buying the apartment. There's the mortgage. Kids' tutoring costs. And even though the price went up, I can't sell — I live there."

Got Gangnam — and Gangnam got her.

choices.text: "But you achieved the goal." — see the positive
choices.result_text:
Lee Minseo smiled briefly. "Yes. I did achieve it."

But that smile was different somehow. {name} wanted to understand the difference. Probably have to get there to know.

choices.text: "Is there something I'm not seeing? Tell me honestly." — ask directly
choices.result_text:
She thought for a moment, then said:
"When you have a goal — you have to be ready for when the goal disappears. That's the hardest part."

It took {name} a while to understand what that meant.

title: The One Who Arrives
description:
Gangnam wasn't far now.

With the number nearly full, a message came from Lee Minseo.
"I heard. They say you're almost there."

They met again at that same cafe.
"Congratulations. I mean it."
Then she went quiet for a moment.
"Remember what I told you back then?"

{name} remembered. 'When you have a goal, prepare for when it disappears.'
Now — he was starting to understand what she meant.

choices.text: "I think I'm starting to get it." — said it honestly
choices.result_text:
Lee Minseo nodded.
"Right? When you arrive, the next question comes. 'So now what.'
But that's not all bad. At least — it's a new question."

For the first time, {name} felt that Gangnam wasn't the end, but the start of the next sentence.

choices.text: "I haven't arrived yet. Don't want to count my chickens." — smiled
choices.result_text:
Lee Minseo laughed. "Fair enough. See it all the way through."

Still, {name} decided to tuck her words away in his bag.
He'd take them out once he got there.
